lines.head: Pale leaves
lines.text: Your pechay leaves are turning pale.

lines.head: Complete?
lines.text: So you buy a sack of complete fertilizer.

lines.head: Complete?
lines.text: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. All three.

lines.head: Only one
lines.text: But your soil may be short of only one.

lines.head: Leyte soils
lines.text: In Leyte, six in ten farms already have plenty of potassium.

lines.head: Wasted
lines.text: Buy more, and that money is wasted.

lines.head: Nitrogen
lines.text: Pale leaves usually point to nitrogen.

lines.head: Nitrogen
lines.text: It keeps leaves green, and leafy crops like pechay need the most.

lines.head: Probe
lines.text: Push the SakaSense probe into moist soil, about ten centimeters deep.

lines.head: Five spots
lines.text: Take five readings across the bed.

lines.head: N · P · K
lines.text: The screen shows your nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

lines.head: Code 4
lines.text: Plus one simple code. Here, code four: nitrogen low.

lines.head: The fix
lines.text: Open Kasaka, and code four gives you the exact fix.

lines.head: 50 grams
lines.text: Just fifty grams of urea per bed. About five tablespoons.

lines.head: Skip
lines.text: Phosphorus and potassium are already good. Skip them.

lines.head: Green again
lines.text: Then watch your pechay turn green again.

lines.head: Test first, then buy
lines.text: SakaSense and the Kasaka app. Test first, then buy.
